text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 - GPU OOMs during prefill observed in runtime-prod-3 across several containers. Alerting oncall-ml and eng-runtime. (auto: pagerduty)

sasha (oncall-ml): got the page, pulling logs now. seeing container restarts every ~90s on node gpu-17.

jamie (sre): I'm seeing node flaps too — kubelet restarting the containers. Kube events show OOMKilled. tagging infra.

mike (eng-runtime): can you paste the OOM trace? curious if it's prefill spike (long prompt) or memory leak.

sasha (oncall-ml): paste of recent stderr from runtime container:
```
[2026-03-15T04:20:12Z] ERROR runtime: cuda: out of memory
requested: 3.16GB, available: 2.28GB
prefill_tokens: 8192, batch_size:1, seq_len:8192
stack: serving/runner.go:412 -> kvcache/prefill.go:89
container restart count=2
```

jamie (sre): that looks like huge prefill window. customer traffic spike with some very long contexts. impact: increased 503s from the long-context route.

tess (support): support ticket stream shows multiple customers complaining about truncated responses and errors. Affected tenants: T-314, T-512, T-771. Reached out with temporary mitigation note.

mike (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations I'm pushing now:
- set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=2048 for runtime-prod-3 pool (hotfix)
- enable per-request prefix eviction so very long prefill requests drop to 2048 tokens
- throttle/queue requests >4096 tokens at the gateway
I'll roll a 10% canary to the pool, verify telemetry, then 100% if stable.

deploy-bot: triggered rollout: runtime-config/prefill-limits -> canary=10%. https://ci.redwood/runtime-deploy/4921 :white_check_mark:

sasha (oncall-ml): verifying logs after canary: within 3m I see fewer OOMs on canaried pods. Node gpu-17 still has one older container restarting.

infra-bot: noticed ephemeral disk pressure on gpu-17; evicting PODs. Suggest cordon + drain then reboot if restarts continue.

jamie (sre): taking gpu-17 out of rotation, draining now. planning a restart if OOMKilled rates persist after config.

mike (eng-runtime): additional mitigation: temporarily route requests with prefills >6000 tokens to cpu-fallback-pool (no GPU) with degraded latency but safer memory profile. Adding gateway rule now.

sasha (oncall-ml): applied gateway rule, sample requests being routed. Telemetry: error rate for long-context endpoint dropped from 6.1% -> 1.2% in the canary region.

tess (support): updated customers T-314/T-512/T-771 with ETA and mitigation steps. They accepted temporary performance hit.

jamie (sre): gpu-17 drained and restarted. After restart, node health looks stable. No further OOMs in last 14m.

mike (eng-runtime): follow-ups (post-incident actions):
- add server-side enforcement of PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS per model by default
- add a runtime metric for prefill memory usage per request
- evaluate KV cache eviction strategy to avoid full-buffering of very long contexts
- add automatic fallback routing when prefill memory > threshold

sasha (oncall-ml): quick runbook notes for handoff:
- incident id: INC-20260315-001
- root cause: unbounded client requests with very large prefill windows causing per-request CUDA allocation > node available memory -> container OOMKilled -> node pod churn
- mitigations applied: PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=2048 hotfix (rolled to 100%), gateway routing to cpu-fallback for >6000 tokens, drained gpu-17
- customer impact: ~4% of requests to /v1/long-context returned 503/err. Tenants T-314, T-512, T-771 experienced degraded/failed calls. Support notified.
- monitoring: watch metrics `oom_killed_count`, `prefill_tokens_hist`, `gpu_memory_alloc_bytes` for any regressions

jamie (sre): handing off to next oncall (mike) at 06:00 UTC. next-oncall checklist:
- confirm PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS remains enforced cluster-wide
- revert cpu-fallback routing only after verifying 48h of stable OOM/Kill=0
- follow up with infra to check kernel logs / GPU driver versions on gpu-17

mike (eng-runtime): accepted handoff. I'll own the follow-ups and a short postmortem draft. Initial hypothesis: no code-level memory leak, just bad client behavior + missing guardrails.

tess (support): I'll coordinate customer follow-ups and include the mitigation timeline.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-001 moved to status: mitigation. Assigned owners: eng-runtime (mike), oncall-ml (sasha), sre (jamie). Please update the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/INC-20260315-001

mike (eng-runtime): leaving a small note for the postmortem: consider default per-request prefill cap in the API and a soft-quotas / rate-limiter that rejects vs crash.

sasha (oncall-ml): thanks all. dropping to watch mode. :thumbsup:

jamie (sre): next update scheduled at handoff or earlier if regression. closing channel when postmortem link posted.
